meta.title: Minesweeper for Kindle & E-Ink — Free, No Download
meta.description: Play free Minesweeper in your browser on Kindle, BOOX or Kobo. No download, no install — classic mine-hunting built for black-and-white e-ink screens.

h1: Minesweeper for Kindle & E-Ink — Free, No Download
tagline: Classic Minesweeper that runs right in your Kindle Paperwhite, Scribe or BOOX browser — no app to install, nothing to download, just open the page and start digging.

steps: Pick a board. Easy is a 9×9 grid with 10 mines, Medium is 11×11 with 24, and Hard is 13×13 with 40. Bigger boards reward patient scanning over fast tapping.

Dig the first square. Your opening tap is always safe — mines are only planted after it, and the square you hit plus all eight of its neighbours are kept mine-free, so an opening move can never blow up.

Read the numbers. Each digit counts the mines in the eight squares around it. A blank square touches no mines, so the game opens whole blank regions for you in one tap, and you only work the numbered edges.

Flag suspected mines. Switch to Flag mode and tap a square to mark it; a flag blocks accidental taps, and the counter above the board shows mines left — the total minus your flags. Tap the same square again to remove a flag.

Chord to go faster. In Dig mode, tap an open number when the flags around it match the digit: every other neighbour opens at once. It is the classic two-tap shortcut for confident players, and it is fully supported here.
Play with keys. Arrow keys move the cursor, Enter or Space digs (or chords an open number), and F flags the square — handy on e-readers with a keyboard attached or when a tap is just too far away.

Beat the clock. The timer starts on your first move and pauses while the page is in the background. Clear every safe square to win — the remaining mines are flagged for you — and your progress is saved automatically if you leave.

rows.note: The built-in browser runs the full game; needs firmware 5.13.7 or newer.
The 10.2-inch screen shows even the 13×13 Hard board at full size with room to spare.
Same browser engine as recent Paperwhites — the game stays black-and-white by design.

rows.device: BOOX (Go, Note, Tab, Palma and similar)
rows.note: Full Chromium browser, the smoothest e-ink experience; keyboard shortcuts work with a paired keyboard.
The built-in browser is dated and may not run the game on every model or firmware version.
No official browser app; third-party options require jailbreaking the tablet.
Pre-2016 experimental browsers can't run modern JavaScript — this page stays readable, but the game won't start.

whyEInk: Minesweeper is a quiet game, and e-ink is a quiet screen. Nothing here animates, flashes or refreshes behind your finger — only the square you touch redraws, as a fast partial update. The fixed black-and-white grid reads like a printed puzzle page in daylight, and long sessions barely touch the battery.

faq.a: Yes — completely. Every board size is free to play, with no account, no paywall and no ads. The site belongs to the E-Ink.me family and runs alongside the free e-reader tools on the main site, so there is nothing to buy and nothing to sign up for.

faq.q: Does it work on my Kindle Paperwhite?
faq.a: If your Paperwhite is a 2021 or later model on firmware 5.13.7 or newer, yes — open the built-in browser, type in the site address and start digging. Older Paperwhites with the early experimental browser can display this page as plain text, but they cannot run the game itself.

faq.q: Do I need to jailbreak my Kindle?
faq.a: No. The game runs entirely in your Kindle's built-in web browser. There is no app to sideload, no hack to apply and no warranty risk — opening a web page is an ordinary thing for a Kindle to do. If the device can load a page, it can play this game.

You need an internet connection the first time you open the page, because the site is delivered as a normal web page rather than a downloadable app. Once it loads, the game runs locally on your device — but e-reader browsers are not built for offline use, so plan on being connected when you start.
